newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas prices rise with cold weather.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas prices rise with cold weather.

text.p: U.S. spot natgas prices remained firm Tuesday, propped up by continuing cold weather in the northeastern and midwestern U.S., sources said.

Gulf Coast gas traded early in the mid-$2.70s but then softened into the low-$2.70s to high-$2.60s shortly before nomination deadlines as forecasters called for warmer temperatures to emerge by next week and additional nuclear units returned to service in the East.
Tempering a more significant rise in prices, traders said, was the reliance on storage supplies, especially in the eastern markets, where inventories are nearly full.
Early estimates for Wednesday's American Gas Association (AGA) weekly storage report have ranged anywhere from minus 30 to plus 15 billion cubic feet.

In the Midcontinent, where buyers may not have the luxury of drawing on plentiful storage supplies, prices gained an additional three to five cents today to the mid-to-high $2.60s, with the higher-priced deals evident early.
Temperatures in the Midwest are expected to be about 10 to 20 degrees below-normal throughout this week, but storage inventories, as reported by AGA last week, are just over 70 percent of capacity.
The Chicago city-gate market was also stronger because of the weather in the $3.03-3.11 area, up about 10 cents from Monday.
In west Texas, where demand has been fairly weak, Permian prices climbed only about two cents to the mid-to-high $2.50s in response to the stronger Midwest and Gulf markets.
At the southern California border, prices were similarly up marginally in the mid-$2.60s to low-$2.70s.

On the opposite coast, New York city-gate prices continued to strengthen as traders reported closing deals in the $3.35-3.50 range. Temperatures in the region are expected to return to seasonable levels by early next week, forecasters said.
